method: spatially explicit land cover change model, carbon emission and extinction debt estimates with time lags
finding: Deforestation from 1950 to 2009 left a carbon emissions debt of at least 8.6 petagrams and an extinction debt above 140 forest species, even if clearing had stopped in 2010.
gap_quote: Tropical deforestation has caused a significant share of carbon emissions and species losses, but historical patterns have rarely been explicitly considered when estimating these impacts [1].

method: machine learning image classification, logistic regression

finding: Dry forest was lost at 1.4 and gained at 0.7 per cent a year, both explained by slope and road distance, and wide intervals suggested equilibrium.
gap_quote: Tropical dry forest is one of the most threatened ecosystems, and it is disappearing at an alarming rate.

method: not stated
predictors: agricultural prices, wages, off-farm employment, roads, technological change, agricultural input prices, household incomes, tenure security, population growth, poverty, national income, economic growth, foreign debt

data: CATHALAC and NASA forest cover estimates

method: random forest, XGBoost, artificial neural network, naive Bayes, multilayer perceptron, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, marginal response curves

gap_quote: Deforestation is a spiralling environmental catastrophe with impervious results for biodiversity, climate change, and human livelihoods, specifically in tropical regions.

method: Landsat time series analysis, household surveys, comparison of intervention and non-intervention domains

gap_quote: Agricultural interventions can help boost food security for poor rural communities but in certain cases can exacerbate deforestation, known as the rebound effect.

period: 20 year series, years not stated, projected to 2030

gap_quote: In the context of emerging international trade regulations on deforestation-free commodities, the drivers of households' deforestation in conservation landscapes are of interest.

data: existing national forest maps, sample points

gap_quote: Des rapports précis et cohérents sur l'évolution de la superficie forestière et des changements d’occupation du sol sont importants dans le contexte de l’accord de Paris où les pays ont l’obligation de soumettre régulièrement leurs rapports sur le bilan émission absorption des gaz à effet de serre.

method: maximum entropy model

place: Cameroon, Bouba-Ndjida National Park, Bénoué National Park

gap_quote: In a context where deforestation poses a major threat to ecosystems, Cameroon—described as “Africa in miniature ” (Tchawa, 2012), is facing significant human pressure that is accelerating the degradation of its natural environments (FAO, 2020).

method: cartographic, descriptive and comparative methods

place: Nigeria, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Democratic Republic of the Congo

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kisangani, Masako, Mbiye, Yoko, Yangambi

gap_quote: Assessing long-term forest fragmentation is essential for understanding the ecological integrity of tropical landscapes.

method: not stated

method: model of election effects on annual deforestation, model type not stated

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Bas-Congo Province, Luki Biosphere Reserve

place: pantropical, including Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and West-Central Africa
method: not stated

gap_quote: Lack of tenure rights, short and uncertain logging concessions, low stumpage values, and inadequate monitoring of logging activities are among the major policy failures that help deplete the tropical forests.

method: not stated
finding: Congo Basin forests remain largely continuous and species rich, but timber exploitation, fires, plantations, hunting, population growth and mining drive deforestation, amid political instability.
gap_quote: Currently however, apart from the present political instability causing massive problems to people and nature alike, factors like timber exploitation, forest fires, plantations, hunting, population growth and mining all contribute greatly to deforestation and loss of biodiversity in the area.

data: Landsat images of 1988, 2001 and 2020, field investigations

gap_quote: The Congo Basin rainforest, the world's second largest continuous tropical forest, lost an estimated 6,000 km² of tree cover per year between 2019 and 2023, much of it driven by illegal clearing that evades optical satellite monitoring under persistent cloud cover.

finding: Baseline runs lost about 200 million ha of forest from 2006 to 2025, and a 6 dollar per tonne carbon incentive or 12 dollar tax would halve deforestation.
gap_quote: Innovative financial mechanisms would be required to help reducing deforestation.

data: remote sensing post-deforestation land use, pantropical 30 m above-ground biomass map

method: country case studies

gap_quote: The endangered bonobo (Pan paniscus), endemic to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), is threatened by hunting and habitat loss.

method: not stated

gap_quote: In comparison to other rainforests around the world, the pressure on biodiversity is comparatively low in the Congo Basin. But land use intensification and climate change are poised to increase the rate of forest loss.

method: qualitative comparison of permanence, additionality, baselines, uncertainty and leakage

place: Amazon, Congo, Indonesia and New Guinea

method: not stated

gap_quote: These rules presently focus on the conversion of forest to agriculture and pasture use, but could be generalized to other land use change conversions.

method: not stated
finding: Congo Basin forests hold highly endemic biodiversity and vital services, and benefit from forest policies and passive protections such as low rural density and poor infrastructure.
